body.estimand_functional: \(P_x(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(p)=A_{D,y}(p)/B_{D,y}(p)\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) on the equality branch

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\) after one certified input and its equality-branch circuit have been fixed.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent draws in the finite cell space \(\Omega\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention \(do(X=x)\) is a causal query, not a randomized sampling arm.
sampling_model.overlap: Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives positive cells and positive recorded marginal denominators at the fixed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisances; \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) and \(\widehat V_n=J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\}J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\) are computed from the fixed certified circuit.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives a sufficient graphical condition for simultaneous identification over a finite SA-MPDAG family.
Theorem 3.6 gives a necessary-and-sufficient criterion and generalized truncated factorization for one MPDAG.
Theorem 8 identifies a DAG factorization component by saturation of local and global Markov ideals.
Theorem 3 minimally enumerates distinct intervention functionals represented by one MPDAG.
IDP is sound and complete for causal-effect identification from one PAG.
A discrete causal query under one specified model compiles to a sharp polynomial program with anytime-valid outer bounds.
Resampling CI statistics and unioning graphwise intervals yields asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed effect after PC discovery.
SP consistently recovers the true MEC under the sparsest Markov representation condition.

body.tldr: Observational discovery can return several non-Markov-equivalent graphs with the same minimum edge count, and selecting one of them can change \(P_x(Y)\). SparseSIM-ID accepts a certified input only after checking that the tied family is nonempty and that a supplied positive rational table realizes the exact CI oracle. It converts every represented DAG's truncated factorization into a rational observed-table circuit and, conditional on the effect-specific rational-positive separation theorem, returns either a common circuit with fixed-order real-radical certificates or a bounded-height rational ambiguity table. The certified four-binary-variable instance is a strict decision-theoretic improvement over the sufficient graphical test of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo, and a pointwise multinomial delta method supplies inference for one fixed certified equality-branch circuit.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification theory gives sufficient graphical conditions but not a necessary common-law test or a positive rational failure witness for tied sparsest outputs.
project_justification.niche: Minimum-edge ties are a structured and operationally important family in which graph-local Markov constraints are redundant, so completeness turns on the narrower algebraic question of whether intervention signatures detect only statistically relevant components of the oracle CI variety.
project_justification.fill: The project restricts attention to checkably nonempty certified inputs, isolates and proves an effect-specific rational-positive separation theorem, packages it into an exhaustive certificate algorithm with explicit size bounds, proves strictness over the closest sufficient graphical test on a certified rational witness, and attaches fixed-input plug-in inference with an explicit sandwich covariance to the common circuit.

body.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (Proceedings of the 42nd ICML, 2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest causal boundary: their SA-MPDAG criterion is sufficient, and their necessity discussion asks for one common density with unequal graphwise effects. Theorem 2 is a strict decision-theoretic tightening on certified tied-sparsest inputs because it decides every query, while Corollary 1 gives a positive rational instance on which their graphical test is undecided and SparseSIM-ID returns a separator. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies the graph-specific bucket truncated factorization adapted here into rational observed-cell circuits. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005, Theorem 8) inform saturation by positive marginal factors, while Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017, Sections 3.1 and 3.3) explain why irrelevant CI components make positivity a separate issue. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) define the tied minimum-edge discovery target without an effect-aware output policy. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3) inform effect quotienting within one MPDAG. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, Section 4.2) inform the success-or-obstruction proof architecture for one PAG. Duarte et al. (2024) inform polynomial compilation and certified optimization. Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) inform the distinction between discovery and estimation uncertainty; Theorem 3 is pointwise for one fixed certified population input and does not claim selection-aware validity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets but does not impose the signs \(p_z>0\), and it does not enforce the nonvanishing blocks associated with zero bits of an exact CI oracle. Therefore \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\) is not by itself a statistical nonidentification certificate. Theorem 1 is the substantive claim that closes exactly this gap for intervention signatures generated by tied minimum-edge families. General rational-point density on arbitrary CI varieties is neither assumed nor claimed.
body.honest_scope: The exact CI oracle, background orientations, query, complete tied minimum-edge family, and a positive rational exact-oracle feasibility witness are fixed certified population inputs; empty graph families and unrealizable exact oracles are outside the accepted domain. Theorem 1 and the rational-atlas question are open and headline-bearing; real-radical computation, certificate checking, and the pointwise fixed-input delta method are supporting results. The four-variable certified table has minimum cell \(1/40\), exactly four elementary CIs, \(50\) I-map DAGs, exactly two four-edge minima in distinct MECs, and intervention probabilities \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). If rational-positive separation fails, a complete algebraic-number witness procedure remains possible but is outside the claimed theorem. When the candidate family is one MPDAG and the oracle model equals that graph's positive Markov model, Theorem 2 reduces to Perkovic's known criterion. Theorem 3 fixes one certified input and one interior law; it makes no uniform claim over changing circuits, and data-driven estimation of the CI oracle or sparsity ties requires separate selection-aware analysis.
